authority_algebra.bottom: ⊥ = NO_AUTHORITY: internal sentinel and evaluation outcome; never issuable, never storable, never 'unrestricted'

invariants.text: Delegation may preserve or reduce already-authorized scope; it never creates, amplifies, infers, recovers, combines or manufactures authority.
For every valid edge: scope(child) <= redelegable_scope(parent) in every dimension; for every chain: A0 >= A1 >= ... >= An.
The only authority roots are HUMAN_OWNER grants issued through the trusted non-agent layer; SYSTEM_POLICY is a ceiling every chain is intersected with, never a grantor.
Identity, title, role, display_name, metadata, provider, model and registration create zero authority.
A delegated ceiling is an upper bound, never a permission result; the Permission Engine still classifies every action.
Every consequential action names exactly one leaf delegation; its lineage is the only authority source considered; no union across lineages.
Delegation records are immutable and append-only; effective state is computed, never stored as mutable status.
Revocation removes whole edges only, is irreversible, and makes every descendant ineffective; descendants are never re-parented.
Delegation never carries, implies or widens approval; approval never mutates or widens a delegation.
Unknown, missing, ambiguous or unparseable security state fails closed; missing never means unlimited; there are no wildcards.
A delegation_id is a reference, never a bearer credential; trust comes only from the trusted store, never from field resemblance or schema validity.
Authority evaluation is deterministic for the same trusted records, system policy, registry state, objective, action requirements and trusted time snapshot.
Delegation cannot authorize modifying the delegation system, Permission/Approval/Budget engines, security contracts, validators, frozen artifacts or migrations as an ordinary change.
Future execution revalidates the complete lineage at the final authorization boundary with a trusted clock.
The authority algebra is closed with an explicit bottom ⊥ (zero authority). ⊥ is never issuable or storable and never means unrestricted. [HR-01]
The requesting principal is a typed PrincipalRef bound once, durably, when the Action is created. No later caller may substitute it, and no default requester holds authority. [HR-03]
Any lifecycle event of the delegator or delegate since issuance permanently ends an edge's effectiveness. Re-enabling never resurrects authority. [HR-04]
Authority is pinned to exact schema, action-vocabulary and objective versions. An absent or unknown dimension grants zero authority. [HR-05, HR-09, HR-10]
System policy is a typed ceiling that only narrows. It is never evaluable alone and never originates authority, and owner roots cannot override it. [HR-07]

proof_obligations.text: No delegation increases any authority dimension.
proof_obligations.test_strategy: Property test: for random parent scope P and random request R, attenuate(P, R) either raises or returns C with leq(C, P) true in every dimension.

proof_obligations.text: Every effective delegation has a valid trusted HUMAN_OWNER root.

proof_obligations.text: Every child delegation is bounded by its complete ancestor chain, recomputed at evaluation, not trusted from issuance.
proof_obligations.test_strategy: Store-tamper test: a record injected past issuance validation with scope wider than its parent's redelegable_scope is REJECTED (LINEAGE_INVALID) by the evaluator's per-hop leq check, never silently clipped (check-not-clip applies at evaluation too).

proof_obligations.text: Revoked or expired upstream authority invalidates dependent effective authority.
proof_obligations.test_strategy: Multi-hop test: revoke/expire each edge of A->B->C->D in turn; every descendant becomes NOT_EFFECTIVE with UPSTREAM_INEFFECTIVE.
Exhaustive enum tests; unknown schema_version/dimension/status/principal kind; missing parent; corrupt lineage.

proof_obligations.text: The lineage keys (root_delegation_id, objective_ref) are identical for every descendant, so a future exact-payload DenialRecord is visible across redelegation. (Downgraded [HR-11]: v0.2.5 does not itself stop a denied intent being requested again.)

proof_obligations.text: Changing provider/model cannot change delegated authority.

proof_obligations.text: Authority evaluation is deterministic for the same trusted inputs.

proof_obligations.text: Every chain is principal-acyclic and continuous: delegate(edge i) == delegator(edge i+1), no principal repeats, self-delegation impossible.

proof_obligations.text: Security-critical records are deeply immutable through all ordinary mutation APIs (B-11) and admitted only as exact-type, revalidated, store-owned snapshots (v0.2.4 B-01).
proof_obligations.test_strategy: Mutation matrix incl. |= and *=; subclass/model_construct/model_copy smuggling fixtures.

proof_obligations.text: The algebra is closed: meet is total on AuthorityScope ∪ {⊥}; ⊥ is never issued, never stored, and never treated as unrestricted. [HR-01]
proof_obligations.test_strategy: Property tests: meet is commutative, associative and idempotent over random scopes, including disjoint sets and differing objectives; meet ≤ both inputs; ⊥ is absorbing; issuance that normalizes to ⊥ is rejected.

proof_obligations.text: The requester is bound once at Action creation and every later check reads that binding; no default requester holds authority. [HR-03]
proof_obligations.test_strategy: Resume or recovery by a caller with a different requester → REQUESTER_UNBOUND; a 'system' or empty requester → NO_EFFECTIVE_DELEGATION.

proof_obligations.text: An edge is effective only if neither delegator nor delegate has had a lifecycle event since issuance; re-enabling never restores it. [HR-04]
proof_obligations.test_strategy: Disable then re-enable at every hop of a 10-hop chain → all descendants stay non-effective.

proof_obligations.text: Version pinning: a record with a different schema_version, vocabulary_version or objective_version grants no authority, and an absent dimension grants zero. [HR-05, HR-09, HR-10]
proof_obligations.test_strategy: v1 record under a v2 evaluator → UNKNOWN_AUTHORITY_DIMENSION; vocabulary bump → VERSION_MISMATCH; objective edit → OBJECTIVE_MISMATCH.

proof_obligations.text: System policy only narrows: no lineage ⇒ ⊥ whatever the ceiling; a root above the ceiling is rejected; tightening the ceiling lowers the effective scope. [HR-07]
proof_obligations.test_strategy: Empty-store evaluation with a permissive ceiling → ⊥; owner P4 root under a P2 ceiling → rejected; tightening after issuance → effective P2.

revocation_threat_matrix.design_response: Revoker must be HUMAN_OWNER, the edge's delegator, or an ancestor delegator in the lineage; otherwise REVOKER_NOT_AUTHORIZED.
Children are not ancestors of their parent edge; and scopes have no separable constraints to revoke (whole-edge only).
Revocation only ever removes edges; effective authority is a meet along one lineage; descendants are never re-parented; removing an edge can never enlarge any lineage's meet.
Effective state of an edge requires every ancestor edge effective (UPSTREAM_INEFFECTIVE).
No cache in v0.2.5; future caches must be invalidated by the revocation watermark.
Revocation keyed by delegation_id is permanent; ids never reused; records carry no status to replay.
Idempotent: first RevocationRecord wins; later attempts are recorded as no-ops and never alter revoked_at.

Issuance of a child and revocation of its parent serialize on the parent edge; if revocation commits first, issuance fails UPSTREAM_INEFFECTIVE; if issuance commits first, the child is immediately ineffective by cascade.
Evaluation reads a consistent snapshot (records + revocations + watermark); result carries the watermark it used; final boundary re-evaluates.

Final-boundary check (C') and execution claim (E) occur in one serialized transaction with the revocation read; revocation after claim cannot retract an in-flight adapter effect (documented residual window).

findings.counterexample: meet({read}@O1, {send}@O1): the intersection ∅ violates the non-empty invariant. meet(·@O1, ·@O2) was "undefined"
findings.impact: The "meet-only algebra" claim was false. An implementer could return `None` for an undefined meet, and `None` might then be read as "no restriction"
findings.remediation: Explicit ⊥ (NO_AUTHORITY), an internal sentinel, never issued or stored; meet made total; `EMPTY_AUTHORITY` reason; DI-15, PO-15, T-45

findings.counterexample: `external_modify` on a HIGH-risk tool → EXTERNAL/HIGH. EXTERNAL/LOW is reachable through a tool declaring EXTERNAL/LOW with `read` support, which contradicts the draft's "unreachable"
findings.impact: The P3/P4 distinction was under-specified and depended on the unstated `max()` risk semantics. A careless mapping (risk ≤ MEDIUM → P3) would under-classify
findings.remediation: §3.7: exact `max(T_floor, T_class)` table; P3 only when positively established; residual tool-misdeclaration risk stated; CR-02 ownership; T-57

findings.counterexample: Plan created with `requested_by="agent.a"`, later resumed by a caller passing `requested_by="agent.b"`. Nothing durable records A. The default requester is `"system"`
findings.impact: Sibling or requester substitution once delegation is integrated. Part I's amendment wrongly implied that today's `requested_by` is trustworthy
findings.root_cause: The requester is a bare, per-call, unpersisted string
findings.remediation: Typed PrincipalRef bound insert-once at Action creation; every later check reads the binding; no default requester; trusted principal context declared as a dependency; DI-16, PO-16, T-46, `REQUESTER_UNBOUND`

findings.counterexample: CEO disabled, then re-enabled. The evaluator reads only current `enabled`, so CTO's delegation silently returns. Without CR-04 there is no atomic revocation
findings.root_cause: Dynamic suspension was the de-facto semantics
findings.remediation: Lifecycle-history rule: any event since `issued_at` permanently ends the edge; re-issuance required; revocation ≠ disable; integration precondition on append-only lifecycle history; DI-17, PO-17, T-47
findings.design_test: disable→enable at every hop of a 10-hop chain

findings.counterexample: v0.2.6 adds tenant scope. The Part I sentence "enforced by their owning systems; delegation does not widen them" lets a v1 record pass the delegation gate for any tenant
findings.root_cause: Two contradictory statements (fail closed vs silent)
findings.remediation: §3.5: absent dimension = zero; exact-version evaluation; no automatic upgrade; no cross-system inference; DI-18, PO-18, T-48

findings.counterexample: One owner authorization event id reused for N root edges, or a root row inserted with a copied event id
findings.impact: Unbounded root minting from a single human act
findings.root_cause: No uniqueness or content binding on the root
findings.remediation: Unique `owner_authorization_event_id`; `root_request_digest`; `issue_root` only on the owner channel; DB integrity as a stated trust assumption; T-49

findings.counterexample: No delegation, P3 ceiling: an implementer computes meet(ceiling) = P3. Owner issues P4 while policy allows P2
findings.impact: System policy acting as a grantor; owner overriding policy
findings.root_cause: The ceiling was untyped, and the root-vs-ceiling rule was unstated
findings.remediation: §3.8: typed SystemPolicyCeiling, not evaluable alone; no lineage ⇒ ⊥; root above ceiling rejected; later tightening applies; override only through a separate policy-management action; `policy_version` recorded; DI-19, PO-19, T-50

findings.counterexample: `execute_action_durably(action, PermissionDecision(ALLOW))` for an external action skips gate C today
findings.impact: Approval bypass today and delegation bypass after integration if C′ runs after A/B
findings.root_cause: The executor trusts the caller's decision
findings.remediation: C′ runs before A/B/C, recomputes permission and delegation, and uses the supplied decision only as a consistency check; T-53

findings.counterexample: Permission Engine re-tiers `external_modify`, or a tool starts using `read` for a sending operation. Old scopes containing the string now cover the new meaning
findings.remediation: `vocabulary_version` pinned in the scope and in the ceiling; any change bumps it; `VERSION_MISMATCH`; T-52

findings.counterexample: Delegation issued for objective O. O's text is later changed from "research suppliers" to "sign supplier contract" with the same id
findings.impact: Authority silently changes meaning; ids could be model-chosen
findings.root_cause: The objective was unversioned and its origin unspecified
findings.remediation: `ObjectiveRef(id, version)`; immutable per version; control-plane origin; no objective store today, so this is an integration precondition; T-54

findings.counterexample: "denied → new agent: YES". A reworded or byte-changed payload evades any hash key, and no DenialRecord exists
findings.root_cause: An exact-hash key was presented as intent persistence
findings.remediation: D-02/D-03/D-05 downgraded to EXACT-PAYLOAD ONLY with a future store; PO-09 downgraded; the v0.2.0 denial rules are stated as unmet

findings.counterexample: In v0.1.3, an agent-originated `financial` action reaches REQUIRE_APPROVAL and a human may approve it. After integration the gate BLOCKs it
findings.impact: An existing workflow is removed without the design saying so, and P5 exclusion was presented as if it were constitutional
findings.root_cause: The draft did not separate policy from constitution
findings.remediation: §3.7: exclusion is a new policy decision (DA-03, Human-Owner approved with rewording); no standing P5; agent P5 proposals stop at the authorization boundary; behavior change recorded; OQ-10

findings.counterexample: The approval-binding (`requesting_agent`) and denial-persistence rows were labeled as resolved or as open dependencies
findings.remediation: §O classification: every row labeled compatible, strengthening, refinement or conflict; two pre-existing conflicts named

findings.counterexample: A tampered record with `redelegable_scope > scope` passes the evaluator, because only `leq(child, parent.redelegable)` was re-checked
findings.remediation: Both `leq`s re-checked at every hop; reject, not clip; parent ordering checked; T-56

findings.remediation: `(kind, id)` required for equality, hash, serialization, cycles, revoker checks and audit

findings.counterexample: Can a revocation be revoked? Does the reason matter?

findings.counterexample: Production code placed at `jarvis/delegation.py` or `app/policy/x.py` with renamed classes passes the checker. Counts were hardcoded

findings.remediation: Canonical record digest stored in the `DELEGATION_ISSUED` audit event and re-verified at evaluation (detects corruption and naive tampering, not a DB-admin attacker who updates both); requires B-11 deep immutability

findings.remediation: **Delegation does not make an unconfigured budget safe.** "Unconfigured = unlimited" is a Budget issue, hardened separately if ever; delegation grants no budget

findings.counterexample: Options A, B, C
